rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly, so the table can be pushed toward stronger transformation coverage: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain because this benchmark is dominated by constant-foldable arithmetic on simple types, exactly the pattern SUB defeats when the folding pass can no longer recover the originals; its low cost/risk weights keep it cheap to apply broadly across the 295 mostly-small template instantiations. BCF and IBR are kept strong (0.75/0.8) but with mid-range RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights so opaque predicates and indirect branches concentrate in the few large functions (main and the test_constant instantiations) where control-flow hiding matters most, instead of bloating hundreds of tiny wrappers. FLA is moderated (0.6) since flattening tiny template-instantiated functions adds size with little analytical value, but remains active for the larger hot functions. ICALL stays high on DiversityGain (0.75) with a moderate CorrectnessRisk weight because indirect call conversion on C++ heavy template code is effective against static call-graph recovery but must be gated on functions with safe call targets. SPLIT is cheap and safe, so it is enabled broadly as a force multiplier that makes FLA/BCF output harder to unify. IGV is kept moderate: global variable encryption adds defense-in-depth against the benchmark's many precomputed constant tables without meaningfully touching the hot loop arithmetic. Overall the table raises security/diversity weights relative to a defensive baseline while keeping cost and risk weights bounded so runtime and size stay within acceptable limits and correctness (already verified in round 0) is preserved.
